title: Single-cell visual proteomics of a minimal bacterium reveals structural coordination of gene expression machineries.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Queried the EMDB (Electron Microscopy Data Bank) search API: at least 100 Mahamid-lab Mycoplasma pneumoniae ribosome maps released 2026-09-23, all subtomogram averages (e.g. EMD-53075 30S consensus, EMD-53613 30S with IF1/IF3). Search capped at 100 rows, so total not confirmed. The EMPIAR (raw image archive) API search returned 404. I did not download any map or tomogram.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Abstract only (paper is paywalled, no PMCID): 140 maps from cryo-ET (cryo-electron tomography) of native and antibiotic-treated cells, covering translation phases. No supplement, data statement or raw-tomogram accession seen.

a1_downloadable.note: EMDB maps are public (seen in API); raw tomograms are probably in EMPIAR, but I could not confirm that.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: There is no table. The output is ~140 3D density maps; any per-particle state label would have to be rebuilt from particle lists and classification results that I did not see deposited as a table.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs would be tomograms or subvolumes, which are raw imaging data, not features.

a4_units_stated.note: Maps carry voxel size in the header (standard EMDB metadata); not checked per file.

a5_enough_rows.note: About 140 maps (from the abstract; at least 100 seen in EMDB). Particle counts per class are unknown.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: Tomogram sets for cryo-ET studies usually run to terabytes; size not verified
a6_fits_laptop.note: Particle-level work needs the raw tomograms and a GPU.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: At least 100 EMDB maps seen against 140 claimed; the search was capped, so this is not a contradiction.

a8_label_provenance.note: Particle state labels come from computational 3D classification (sorting particles by shape in software), so they are the output of an algorithm rather than an independent measurement.

backbone.name: none suitable (no freeze-and-head backbone for cryo-ET subvolumes in the approved list)

honest_claim_h3: A model could at best re-sort ribosome particles from one bacterium's tomograms into the states the authors' own classification software already defined.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use 3D images of single ribosomes inside bacterial cells to predict which stage of protein-making each ribosome is in.
plain_idea.train_on: Small 3D image boxes cut out of electron tomograms (3D microscope images) of Mycoplasma pneumoniae cells; number of particles unknown.
plain_idea.predict: The translation stage (start, elongation, recycling) for each ribosome; the 'true' answer comes from the authors' computational classification, not from a separate measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Faster particle sorting would help cryo-ET labs, but this needs raw tomograms, a GPU and labels that come from software, so it doesn't fit this project.

ml_idea: Classify subtomogram particles into translation states; not feasible here because there is no label table, the data is terabyte-scale imaging and the labels come from classification software.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; this is a cryo-ET imaging dataset, not tabular data.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Check whether particle coordinates with per-particle class labels were deposited (EMPIAR or a supplement); none were seen.

verdict_reason: A structural-biology imaging resource (about 140 cryo-ET density maps in EMDB) with no label table. Fails A2, A3, A5, A6 and A8: labels would need rebuilding from software classifications, raw data is terabyte-scale and needs a GPU.
